statusDefinitions.methodImplemented: A public client method exists for this operation.
statusDefinitions.typeCoverage: complete means common request and response options have dedicated exported types; partial means a generic record or escape hatch remains.
statusDefinitions.unitTests: present means at least one unit test covers the method or shared transport path; it does not mean every action is covered.
statusDefinitions.integrationTests: tested means the exact operation behavior has passed an integration test on every pinned Solr version listed as tested; partial means some versions or behavior are tested; not-run means no real Solr server test has been executed for the operation.

entries.notes: Document add is exercised in the CRUD smoke test on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Named SolrUpdateOptions now expose overwrite, commitWithin, and SolrCloud _route_ serialization; request parameter serialization and invalid values are covered by unit tests. SolrCloud integration tests verify add/update route behavior on an implicit-router collection using shard-scoped query read-back, and verify commitWithin search visibility without a manual commit on the pinned _default configset, across Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. The commitWithin test asserts bounded eventual visibility only; hard/soft commit behavior remains controlled by server configuration. Field-specific SolrAtomicUpdateOperation and SolrAtomicUpdateDocument types plus atomicUpdate() support set, add, add-distinct, remove, removeregex, and numeric inc. Unit, consumer type, and pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0 integration tests cover atomic updates. Single JSON documents use /update/json/docs; arrays use /update. Both forms are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. commitWithin is a scheduling hint whose hard/soft behavior is controlled by Solr's commitWithin configuration; the client does not force either commit type. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Unit tests assert the single-document, document-array, and command-map JSON endpoint selection, typed response header, and HTTP error propagation. Unit tests assert single-document, document-array, and command-map endpoint selection, typed response headers, and HTTP error propagation.  Nested parent/child/grandchild JSON document indexing and exact Unicode/multi-valued field read-back are covered by test/integration/solr-document-fidelity.test.ts and passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 in CI run #42392182590. Nested documents must be sent using the array form add([document]) so the request uses /update; Solr's /update/json/docs convenience path flattens complex JSON by default. See docs/update.md and ADR 0003. Nested parent/child/grandchild document round-trip and Unicode/multi-valued field round-trip passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 in CI run #42392182590.
Field-specific atomic update modifiers are covered by unit/type assertions and integration tests on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

SolrCloud CREATE/LIST/DELETE, alias lifecycle, implicit-router shard lifecycle, named ADDREPLICA/DELETEREPLICA lifecycle, replica property add/delete and BALANCESHARDUNIQUE responses, plus multi-node MOVEREPLICA and REBALANCELEADERS leader reassignment are tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #177, #192, #209, and PR #142 CI #224). MOVEREPLICA verifies the named replica becomes active on a different live node. REBALANCELEADERS assigns preferredLeader to an active non-leader and verifies it becomes shard leader. Distinct snapshot operations and some cluster-state response details remain unverified. The BACKUP/LISTBACKUP/RESTORE/DELETEBACKUP and async status flow described below is integration-tested; this does not certify every snapshot action or response field. Additional operation evidence: Typed SolrCloud collection backup/restore actions and asynchronous REQUESTSTATUS/DELETESTATUS tracking. Full backup, list, restore, query read-back, and delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 with a shared local filesystem volume mounted on both SolrCloud nodes. S3 and other external repositories are not certified. LISTALIASES defaults to SolrCollectionAliasesResponse; CREATEALIAS/DELETEALIAS default to SolrCollectionAliasResponse; CLUSTERSTATUS defaults to SolrClusterStatusResponse with extensible collection/shard/replica models. Filtered cluster status and unobserved version-specific fields remain optional/open. CREATESHARD/DELETESHARD now default to SolrCollectionShardOperationResponse and remain integration-tested on all pinned versions. SPLITSHARD has a typed V1 split.key contract (shard or routing-key mode). MIGRATE uses V1 collection/split.key/target.collection/forward.timeout/async parameters and the same response envelope. Both now have opt-in asynchronous integration checks that require SOLR_DESTRUCTIVE_OPT_IN=true, a loopback endpoint, SOLR_CLOUD=true, SOLR_MULTINODE=true, and disposable collections; the manual workflow provisions its own two-node cluster. The tests verify child-shard state and document read-back after split, and target document read-back after migration. The opt-in workflow has not yet been executed, so both operations remain runtime-unverified. Abort, partial-failure recovery, and concurrent-write behavior are not certified. RELOAD now has exact action-specific serialization and isolated collection integration coverage on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. MODIFYCOLLECTION, ADDROLE, and REMOVEROLE now have dedicated serialization and consumer type fixtures; MODIFYCOLLECTION remains runtime-unverified because it mutates collection policy, while role actions remain runtime-unverified because they mutate cluster-wide node role assignments. Named response contracts now cover every action literal: LIST uses SolrCollectionListResponse; CREATE/DELETE/RELOAD/MODIFYCOLLECTION use SolrCollectionAdminResponse; replica lifecycle, movement, balancing, and property actions use SolrCollectionReplicaResponse; ADDROLE/REMOVEROLE use SolrCollectionRoleResponse. CollectionAdminResponse<A> selects the default contract from the action literal while explicit caller generics remain supported. These are extensible response envelopes, not a claim that all action-specific payload fields or all actions are runtime-certified. FORCELEADER is now a separate typed V1 action with exact query serialization and consumer type coverage; its per-version runtime status is recorded independently as unverified until stale-replica fault injection is completed.

Typed SolrExportParams requires fl and sort, supports filter query arrays, raw or structured sort expressions, batchSize, response writer selection, optional local expr, and customParams. export() returns the raw backpressure-aware Response. Sort fields must be single-valued docValues int/long/float/double/string fields; fl additionally supports date/boolean and multi-valued fields. includeStoredFields=true is runtime-tested specifically on Solr 10.1.0: the integration test reads back a stored-only field. No runtime support claim is made for Solr 8.11.4 or 9.11.0. The general raw Export response flow is independently tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0; unit tests cover typed serialization.

Generic SolrResponse<TDocument> and SolrQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> types expose document metadata, classic facet counts, caller-shaped JSON facets, highlighting, grouping, stats, and debug sections. Consumer compile tests verify document inference and response-section property types. Basic query serialization and document retrieval plus cursorMark multi-page traversal are tested on the pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; typed declarations do not certify every optional response section at runtime. Typed classic Facet Component options cover field facets and per-field limit/offset/sort/mincount/missing/prefix/method overrides, query facets, and numeric/date range facets with include/other/hardend and filter/dv methods. Solr date bucketing uses range facets; legacy facet.date parameters were removed in Solr 6. Integration coverage asserts field/query counts and numeric/date range response sections on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed highlighting options cover field selection, highlighter method, snippet/fragment sizing, field matching, alternate fields, phrase and multi-term highlighting, encoders/tags, and per-field overrides. Unit and consumer type tests cover parameter serialization and invalid values; integration tests verify returned snippets on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed Result Grouping options cover group.field, group.func, group.query, per-group limit/offset/sort, group format/main/ngroups/truncate/facet/cache settings; typed grouped response models expose matches, group counts, and per-group document lists. Typed collapse and expand options serialize the Collapsing Query Parser filter and Expand component parameters, with expanded document maps in the response. Standalone integration tests verify field grouping, group sorting, collapse selection, and expansion on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Function grouping and collapse remain subject to Solr's documented distributed/shard-local limitations. Typed Stats Component options support repeated fields, per-field local statistic selection, percentiles, cardinality, tag/key/excludeTags, global stats facets, and calcDistinct. SolrFieldStats response models include nested facet breakdowns, percentiles, and cardinality. Unit and consumer type tests cover encoding and response properties; integration tests verify numeric aggregates, distinct values/counts, cardinality, and category breakdowns on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed MoreLikeThis Search Component options cover field selection, result count, term/document-frequency thresholds, word/token/query-term limits, boosting, query fields, and interesting terms. Unit and consumer type tests cover serialization and response typing; integration tests verify similar-document results on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Geospatial geofilt/bbox filters and geodist sorting are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 using an isolated LatLonPointSpatialField and deterministic nearby/far points; assertions verify inclusion/exclusion and nearest-to-farthest ordering. SpellCheck is an optional server-side component; the client only serializes request options and types its response, and never mutates dictionary or request-handler configuration. The configured default-handler SpellCheck integration test verifies indexed suggestions, frequencies, and a corrected collation; it passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 in CI run #42392182590. Long query parameter preservation on the current GET contract (no automatic GET-to-POST switching) is unit-tested in test/transport-serialization.test.ts. Nested-document child-transformer and Unicode read-back assertions in test/integration/solr-document-fidelity.test.ts passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 in CI run #42392182590; long query preservation is covered by transport unit tests. No automatic GET-to-POST fallback is implemented. Suggester is modelled as an optional query component because it is attached to a deployment-configured SearchHandler; typed dictionary/query/count/context/build/reload parameters and dictionary/query-keyed responses are covered by unit and consumer type tests. The disposable configured-handler Suggester integration test verifies indexed terms and finite weights; it passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 in CI run #42392182590.

Typed single-ID and multi-ID requests use distinct generic response shapes. The API supports field selection, repeated filter queries, custom Solr parameters, and shared request controls. Unit tests cover URL/query serialization, cancellation propagation, reserved-parameter protection, and invalid ID/filter/field values; consumer type fixtures cover valid and invalid request forms. The integration test in test/integration/solr-get.test.ts verifies uncommitted single- and multi-ID read-after-write behavior before the searcher view is updated, including field selection, on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. All three versions passed in CI run #42392182590.

Typed V1 ReplicationHandler commands for enablereplication, disablereplication, indexversion, fetchindex, abortfetch, snappull, abort, enablepoll, disablepoll, details, filelist, backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup; replicationFile() returns raw filecontent streams. Live integration coverage on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 covers indexversion, details, filelist, filecontent, leader enable/disable, and a disposable two-core leader/follower fetch using fetchindex with follower query read-back passed the full standalone/security matrix on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 (CI #640). A bounded disposable-core in-progress abort test passes on Solr 9.11.0 and 10.1.0. Core-level backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are integration-tested on all three pinned versions. Filelist uses the generation returned by newer Solr indexversion responses and falls back to the legacy indexversion parameter when that field is absent. Additional operation evidence: Core-level ReplicationHandler backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are typed. Backup defaults to the core dataDir; restore status is polled with restorestatus. Full backup/restore/read-back/delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Custom filesystem locations must be permitted by server allowPaths.

Generic escape hatch. It does not imply typed support for every Solr endpoint. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction. Generic custom-handler request tests verify repeated query parameter preservation and extensible unknown JSON response fields in test/raw-request.test.ts. Generic custom-handler extensibility, repeated query parameters, and preservation of unknown plugin response fields are covered by raw-request unit tests. Optional `SolrClientConfig.jsonCodec` applies a caller-supplied parser to successful and structured error JSON payloads and a serializer to JSON request bodies. Tests cover exact BigInt round-trip above 2^53-1, normal numbers, decimals, arrays, nested objects, malformed JSON fallback, HTTP errors, and unchanged native defaults. This is client-side behavior and does not carry Solr server-version certification.

Generic raw-response escape hatch using the shared Solr transport. Supports typed methods, query parameters, headers, request bodies, cancellation, timeouts, retry policy, configured validation, and standard Solr error classes. Relative paths and same-origin absolute URLs are supported; cross-origin absolute URLs, embedded credentials, and fragments are rejected before Fetch to prevent credential leakage. String bodies are passed through unchanged when callers supply an explicit Content-Type. Custom endpoint behavior is unverified on Solr 8/9/10 until endpoint-specific integration tests are added. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction. When `requestRaw()` receives a non-string JSON body or an HTTP error response, it uses the configured JSON codec. Explicit string bodies and successful raw response streams bypass parsing/serialization and remain unchanged.

Consumes an AsyncIterable<SolrDocument> and emits a valid top-level JSON array through a Web ReadableStream with highWaterMark 1. Serializes and validates one document at a time, reuses the configured JSON codec and shared request controls, propagates producer/validation errors, HTTP failures, timeout and caller/consumer cancellation, closes the iterator, and disables retries for the non-replayable POST body. Consumer type fixtures assert default/custom response generics and reject synchronous iterables plus invalid numeric option types. Unit tests explicitly cover slow producers, a slow consumer with bounded pull-ahead, framing, empty input, per-document validation, shared auth/headers/request defaults, HTTP errors, timeout/cancellation cleanup, codec use, and no retries. A deterministic 250-document pinned Solr integration test verifies count/order read-back on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Full combined CI run #42376175065 passed 30/30 jobs across Node.js 20/22/24 and standalone, authenticated, and SolrCloud matrices; the standalone job logs confirm 250-document read-back on each pinned image. Partial ingestion is possible if the source or connection fails after the server has accepted a prefix; the operation is not atomic and does not auto-commit.

V1 expert-level shard leader recovery action. Exact collection/shard query serialization and ForceLeaderParams/SolrCollectionShardOperationResponse inference are unit/type-tested. A dedicated manual-only test creates a two-replica collection, commits a baseline, stops the follower during acknowledged writes, stops the old leader, promotes the stale replica, and verifies the data-loss boundary. It validates workflow-owned container labels, Solr image tags, dedicated Docker network, and loopback-only host ports; an independent ZooKeeper container remains running. The workflow has not yet been manually dispatched, so integrationTests remains not-run and all pinned versions remain unverified.

Low-level JSON request escape hatch only. The caller owns operation-specific request/response contracts. Shared transport applies auth, defaults, timeout, cancellation, retry, validation and JSON codec. No operation-specific runtime compatibility is claimed.
Low-level raw-response escape hatch only. The caller owns operation-specific request/response contracts. No operation-specific runtime compatibility is claimed.

Explicit V2 read-only contract distinct from V1 Core Admin types. The exact list/status operations are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 (CI run #42861195999; test/integration/solr-v2-core-admin.test.ts). This certifies only list and status: reload, rename, and unload remain runtime-unverified on Solr 8.11.4 and are tracked independently. This API is for standalone/user-managed cores, not SolrCloud collection management.

Explicit V2 contract distinct from V1 CoreAdmin types. Official Solr 9.11 and 10.1 references document this V2 route; the Solr 8.11 CoreAdmin guide documents V1, while the separate 8.11 V2 guide lists the V2 Core Admin route family; runtime verification on pinned 8.11.4 is pending. Runtime tests cover pinned 9.11.0 and 10.1.0, including authenticated/anonymous access. This API is for standalone/user-managed cores, not SolrCloud collection management. POST has no request body.

Explicit V2 contract distinct from V1 CoreAdmin types. Official Solr 9.11 and 10.1 references document this V2 route; the Solr 8.11 CoreAdmin guide documents V1, while the separate 8.11 V2 guide lists the V2 Core Admin route family; runtime verification on pinned 8.11.4 is pending. Runtime tests cover pinned 9.11.0 and 10.1.0, including authenticated/anonymous access. This API is for standalone/user-managed cores, not SolrCloud collection management. Optional deleteIndex/deleteDataDir/deleteInstanceDir flags default to false.

Read-only SolrCloud collection-name discovery. GET /api/collections is runtime-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 in CI run #43211482752 across Node.js 22/24/26. The test creates an isolated collection and verifies it appears in the V2 list. Uses the shared V2 transport.

Typed post-Solr-9.3 create body with required name/config and common shard/replica fields. Exact unit serialization and consumer type fixtures are present. Runtime and security checks are pending; Solr 8.11 legacy command-envelope payload is intentionally not supported.
V2 collection deletion with explicit optional directory-deletion query flags. Unit serialization and consumer type fixtures are present. Runtime and security checks are pending; no V1 fallback.
REST-style V2 collection reload route documented from Solr 9.3. Unit serialization and consumer type fixtures are present. Runtime and security checks are pending; Solr 8.11 is not claimed.

Read-only per-collection status with narrowly typed common flags and an extensible response. The V2 CollectionStatus route was introduced in Solr 9.3, so pinned Solr 8.11.4 is explicitly not claimed/skipped; runtime tests pass on pinned 9.11.0 and 10.1.0 in CI run #43008748363. This is not full parity with every V1 COLSTATUS detail/size-analysis option.

Read-only cluster discovery. GET CLUSTERSTATUS at /api/cluster is documented from Solr 9.11; pinned Solr 8.11.4 is explicitly not claimed/skipped. Runtime tests pass on pinned 9.11.0 and 10.1.0 in CI run #43008748363; response preserves unknown fields.

Adds one or more replicas to an exact shard, or uses the collection-level shards route with route selector. Supports node/nodeSet, NRT/TLOG/PULL type, replica counts, waitForFinalState, and async. REST-style route documented from Solr 9.0; Solr 8.11.4 not claimed. Unit/type and isolated topology/security tests added; runtime evidence pending.

Deletes only the explicitly named replica. Unlike Solr defaults, the client defaults deleteInstanceDir/deleteDataDir/deleteIndex to false to preserve on-disk data; each deletion flag requires explicit opt-in. Supports onlyIfDown, followAliases, and async. REST-style route documented from Solr 9.0; Solr 8.11.4 not claimed. Unit/type and isolated topology/security tests added; runtime evidence pending.

Read-only V2 alias discovery, distinct from V1 LISTALIASES. The exact GET list route and response shape are documented in Solr 9.2, 9.11, and 10.1 guides. Integration and BasicAuth coverage passed on pinned Solr 9.11.0 and 10.1.0 in CI #43211482752; Solr 8.11.4 is explicitly unclaimed.

Read one alias and its collection targets/properties. The documented detail GET is used directly when available; pinned Solr 10.1.0 returns 405 (Allow: DELETE,OPTIONS), so the client falls back only on 405 to the V2 alias-list response. This V2-only compatibility path and the direct route passed on pinned Solr 9.11.0/10.1.0 in CI #43211482752. Solr 8.11.4 is explicitly unclaimed.

Create or replace a standard alias using the documented V2 {name, collections[]} request body. The redesigned route is documented from Solr 9.3; Solr 8.11.4 legacy alias commands are not mapped or claimed. Unit/type and disposable SolrCloud/security tests are present; runtime and BasicAuth evidence remains pending.

Delete only the alias, not its backing collections. Supports the documented async query parameter. The redesigned route is documented from Solr 9.3; Solr 8.11.4 is not claimed. Runtime and security evidence remains pending.
Read all metadata properties for one alias using the documented Solr 9.3+ property subresource. Solr 8.11.4 is not claimed; runtime evidence pending.
Read one metadata property using the documented Solr 9.3+ property subresource. Solr 8.11.4 is not claimed; runtime evidence pending.
Set a map of metadata properties using the {properties} JSON body and optional async query parameter. Solr 9.3+ route; Solr 8.11.4 is not claimed; runtime evidence pending.
Set one metadata property using the {value} JSON body and optional async query parameter. Solr 9.3+ route; Solr 8.11.4 is not claimed; runtime evidence pending.
Delete one metadata property with the property-level DELETE route and optional async query parameter. Solr 9.3+ route; Solr 8.11.4 is not claimed; runtime evidence pending.

Typed REST-style collection backup contract introduced by the Solr 9.3 V2 route redesign. Solr 8.11.4's older command envelope is intentionally not mapped. Unit serialization, consumer type fixtures, and an isolated SolrCloud read-back test are present; runtime and BasicAuth route-probe evidence is pending CI.

Typed REST-style collection backup contract introduced by the Solr 9.3 V2 route redesign. Solr 8.11.4's older command envelope is intentionally not mapped. Unit serialization, consumer type fixtures, and an isolated SolrCloud read-back test are present; runtime and BasicAuth route-probe evidence is pending CI.

Deletes exactly one backup point by numeric ID and requires the same repository location used for creation. This is a permanent storage mutation; no bulk retainLatest or purgeUnused operation is included in this first slice. Runtime and BasicAuth evidence is pending.

Restores a selected backup point into an existing or newly created collection. Restore replaces target index contents; the caller must select a compatible or disposable target. Optional backupId is sent as a query parameter and create-collection options use the documented V2 body shape. Runtime and BasicAuth evidence is pending.
